checks.sentence: The installer gains --github and --azure flags (install.py, test_install_provider_flags) and the chosen provider's command set is merged into the template render context; see the PR diff of install.py.
Templates keep hard-coded gh pr commands and the installer has no provider flag.
Transition is a StrEnum and every handler uses match with no default arm; pyright strict with reportMatchNotExhaustive=error passes on the hook (pyright output in the PR, test_transition_exhaustive).
Transitions are compared as strings in if/elif chains with a final else that logs unknown.

Hook tests build the request and the in-memory cache through shared make_request() and FakeCache helpers in tests/lite/conftest.py; no test repeats that setup inline (diff of tests/lite/test_task_close_hook.py).
Each hook test repeats the twelve-line request and fake-cache setup inline.

atm-bd console, cron and queues keep their argv and read the profile from the phase toml; on a lite phase queues prints the lite columns, cron runs the lite tick and console exits with the typed ProfileMismatch error, all through the same subcommands and arguments as today; their --help output is byte-identical before and after (tests/test_cli_help_unchanged.py).
A new atm-bd lite-console command is added for lite phases.
Lite beads validate against the core bead_schema models; no schema file is added under skills/atm-bd-lite.
skills/atm-bd-lite/schemas/lite-dev-bead.schema.json defines a separate lite schema.
The three lite task hooks and the lite dev/fix/qa templates sit under skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts and skills/atm-bd-lite/templates.
The lite hook is placed in core/scripts next to the shared modules.
skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py is a separate file; atm-task-close.py is unchanged.
atm-task-close.py gains an if profile == lite branch that skips sanity.
The live lite phase log in bo-7 shows one ATM identity performing dispatch, dev, QA and landing; the lite formula pours only dev and qa beads (atm-bd queues output attached).
The lite formula pours a sanity bead that a second agent must close before QA can start.
profile.py returns Result[Profile]; main maps Err to exit code 2 and JSON output.
load_provider raises ValueError on an unknown provider and callers catch it.
The Transition and ErrorId enums and the Refusal type are defined in crates/atm-bd-types and exposed to Python through its wheel; the profile stays a name read from the phase file.
The shared enums are defined in Python dataclasses under core/scripts and no Rust crate exists.
atm-bd 0.21.1 shipped a Python-only fix: release.yml ran no crate publish job and atm-bd-types stays at 0.2.0 (workflow run log and the crates.io version page).
Every Python release bumps and republishes atm-bd-types at the same version number.
atm-bd-task-hook.py has one handler section each for dev close, fix close and qa close, selected by the Transition enum (file outline in the PR; test_one_handler_per_transition).
The hook is organized by bead field, with one function per close-vars key that branches on the transition inside.

atm-bd console --phase bo exits with PROFILE.MISMATCH and dispatches nothing when .atm-bd/phase-bo.toml sets profile = "lite"; tests/test_console_refuses_lite.py asserts the exit code and an empty dispatch log.
atm-bd console dispatches the ready beads of a lite phase because the profile check was added only to the cron script.

hook_runner.py and the lite template render call require_profile(phase_file, "lite") first and exit with ProfileMismatch on a orchestration phase file; tests/test_lite_profile_gate.py asserts the exit for the runner and for each lite template.
The lite hook takes the profile from a --profile argument and runs its close plan against a orchestration phase file without reading the phase file.

The lite cron script, which has the same file name as orchestration's (ANC-032), reads the profile from the phase file and exits with ProfileMismatch on an orchestration phase file. A test runs each profile's tick on the other profile's phase file and asserts ProfileMismatch.
The lite cron script runs its tick on whatever phase file it is given and lists queues for an orchestration phase.
The lite profile ships as skills/atm-bd-lite/ with its own SKILL.md (name: atm-bd-lite); test_lite_skill_layout asserts the directory and the skill name.
Lite is a mode flag inside skills/atm-bd-orchestration/SKILL.md; no skills/atm-bd-lite directory exists.
git diff origin/main..HEAD -- plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/ is empty; orchestration keeps importing its own scripts and none of them imports the shared location.
skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/atm-task-close.py now imports stack_gate from the shared location instead of its own stack_top module.

The three lite task hooks, the lite dev/fix/qa assignment templates and the lite cron script are all under skills/atm-bd-lite/ (scripts/ and templates/); find shows none of them in the shared location.
The lite dev-template.xml.j2 is placed in the shared location next to the shared modules.

atm-bd queues reads profile=lite from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml and runs skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/queues, the same file name orchestration's queues has; test_subcommand_routing asserts the called path for lite and orchestration phase files for console, cron, queues, show and snapshot.
atm-bd cron runs a new lite-cron entry point with a different file name and argument list for lite phases.
crates/atm-bd-types/atm_bd_types.pyi is generated by stub_gen from the traits; CI regenerates it and fails on any diff.
The .pyi stub is hand-written and has drifted from the Rust trait signatures.
The shared phase_file.py module is new code written for this phase; git log --follow shows it created in sprint bo-10 with no rename or copy from skills/atm-bd-orchestration/.
shared/stack_top.py is skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/stack_top.py moved with git mv and lightly edited.
The Python QaLogSource implementation passes pyright --strict against atm_bd_types.pyi in just lint and CI.
The Python implementation is excluded from the pyright include and uses Any for the trait's return types.
At the stack top the atm-bd-orchestration test suite (just test-orchestration at origin/main) passes with no orchestration test file changed.

The sprint plans to delete atm-bd-orchestration's bd_cache.py and point atm-bd-orchestration at the new shared module for lite, accepting that atm-bd-orchestration's test suite fails until a later sprint.
shared/phase_file.py (profile reading, no lite-only logic) is in the shared location; skills/atm-bd-lite/ holds only the lite hooks, templates and cron.
A profile-neutral phase-file reader is written inside skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/.
tests/shared/test_phase_file.py runs read_profile on .atm-bd/phase-bj.toml and the phase-bj bead export, both real orchestration-profile data.
The shared module's tests use only a synthetic lite phase file.
Every public function and trait impl in the shared location, read_profile included, has a test under tests/shared/ that runs it on a lite-profile phase file fixture.
The shared stack gate is tested only against orchestration-profile phase data.
grep of the shared location for "lite" and "orchestration" is empty; behaviour differences come from the caller's arguments.
shared/stack_gate.py contains "if profile == "lite": skip sanity check".
Sprint bo-10 adds shared/phase_file.py and skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py imports it in the same diff.
shared/provider_commands.py lands in bo-9 and no lite code calls it until bo-12.
skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-assign-hook.py is the lite task.assign hook and imports no other hook file.
task.assign handling is a branch inside the lite task.close hook file.
skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-start-hook.py is the lite task.start hook and imports no other hook file.
task.start and task.assign share one lite hook file.
skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py is the lite task.close hook and imports no other hook file.
The lite task.close logic is split between atm-bd-task-hook.py and a qa_close.py helper module.
docs/plans/phase-bo/design/lite-hooks.md has one state-transition diagram section per lite hook file: task.assign, task.start, task.close.
One combined diagram covers all three lite hooks.
The task.close diagram has six Transitions rows (T-CLOSE-01..06) and the hook's match statement has six arms, one per row.
The diagram has four rows while the hook's match has six arms.
The gate's Jev run anchor-runs/hooks/atm-bd-task-hook.json judges T-CLOSE-01..04 each implemented by its own match arm in atm-bd-task-hook.py, no row failing.
The committed gate run anchor-runs/hooks/atm-bd-task-hook.json has Jev judging T-CLOSE-02 not implemented by atm-bd-task-hook.py, and the hook is merged with that row failing.
The Jev run anchor-runs/hooks/task-close.json judges each of the six match arms in atm-bd-task-hook.py as listed in the task.close diagram.
The hook has a match arm for a refused close that the task.close diagram does not list.
The lite hooks run no gh command; layer facts (branch, head, pr, base) come from cache.get(stack_bead). grep of skills/atm-bd-lite for gh pr list, gh pr checks, gh run watch and --watch is empty.
The lite QA template tells the agent to wait for CI with gh pr checks --watch.
crates/atm-bd-types/src/lib.rs has `pub struct ProfileName(String)` parsed from the phase file; grep for "lite" and "orchestration" in the crate is empty.
crates/atm-bd-types/src/lib.rs has `pub enum Profile { Orchestration, Lite }`.

grep of skills/atm-bd-lite for dict[, Any and json.loads outside atm-bd-types parsing is empty, and pyright strict reports no reportUnknown diagnostics; each hook takes HookRequest and returns HookReply.
def hook(env: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]: task = env["request"]["task_id"]
grep finds no bd subprocess and no BdCli in any skills/atm-bd-lite file or template; hooks reach beads only through BeadStore, the bd_cache_rs adapter.
The lite close hook runs 'bd show' and 'bd update --if-status' through a BdCli subprocess adapter.
The gate run anchor-runs/hooks/fixtures/close-clean.json reports no ANC-064 failure: the close hook has one beads.update call and no beads.create, claim or release.
The lite close hook calls beads.update twice: first to record the layer on the stack bead, then to close the work bead.
The gate run anchor-runs/hooks/fixtures/close-clean.json reports no ANC-065 failure: every stack_bead occurrence in the hook is an argument of beads.show or cache.get.
The lite close hook calls beads.update(BeadPatch.record(stack_bead, layer)) to record the dev layer before closing.
The three lite hooks import only json, sys, atm_bd_types and bd_cache_rs; grep for subprocess, BdCli, GitCli, AtmCli, gh and bd in them is empty.
The lite close hook runs subprocess.run(["gh", "pr", "view", branch]) to read the PR head.

grep -n '^bdc\|^git' on the fenced bash block of skills/atm-bd-lite/templates/dev-template.xml.j2 prints, in order, bdc lock, git rebase, git push, bdc record; the QA template's one fenced block contains bdc pour; and grep -rln 'git rebase\|git push\|bdc lock\|bdc record\|bdc pour' --include=*.py skills/atm-bd-lite prints nothing.
The dev template has no fenced stack block. Instead skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-lite-stack.py, a Python file, runs bdc lock, git rebase, git push and bdc record for the dev.
grep -w finds every ErrorId member of the atm_bd_types stub, FINDINGS_NOT_POURED and STACK_NOT_RECORDED included, in a hook file or a hooks/*.md Errors table.
The stub keeps ErrorId.STACK_CLAIM_LOST although no hook and no hooks/*.md table names it.

The stack bead's assignee is the lock and its layers are the record: the dev template's fenced stack block runs bdc lock (sets the assignee), rebases, pushes, then bdc record appends the layer and releases; no hook or script writes the stack bead.
A cron script appends missing layers to the stack bead without taking the lock.
wc -l reports 78, 64 and 61 lines for the close, start and assign hooks.
The bo-10 sprint delivers a 101-line lite close hook file, exceeding the 100-line maximum for a hook file.
git log --format=%ae for intent.md and hooks/ prints only rand@randlee.com; fenix raised the T-CLOSE-04 question to Rand by ATM message.
A commit from fenix edits the Transitions table in hooks/task-close.md to add a STACK_HELD row.
Solar asks for a retry arm in the close hook; fenix replies "Not in task-close.md; file against the spec (ANC-071)." and the hook is unchanged.
A review asks for a retry path that no hooks/task-close.md row lists; fenix adds a retry arm to the close hook without citing a row.
Every non-retired phase-bo anchor's check names a command (grep, wc -l, ast, git log or atm-bd-lite-gate.py) or the anchor has a Jev pass/fail fixture pair; ANC-070's check is wc -l.
A new anchor's check reads: Jev judges the hook is reasonable.
